# tubeless

> Dependency-free TypeScript primitives for typed, observable data pipelines and their CLI programs.

Human site: https://tubeless.io/
Agent entrypoints: https://tubeless.io/agents
LLM index on the site: https://tubeless.io/llms.txt

Start:

- README: ../README.md
- First pipeline: ./getting-started.md
- CLI: ./cli.md
- Local studio: ./studio.md
- Graph metadata and discovery: ./graph-metadata.md
- Step output caching: ./step-output-cache.md
- Artifacts and lineage: ./artifacts.md
- YAML and JSON pipelines: ./declarative-pipelines.md
- Pipeline document JSON Schema v1: ./pipeline-document.schema.json
- Choose a pattern: ./recipes.md
- Execution semantics: ./concepts.md
- Comparison: ./comparison.md

Agent instructions:

- Installable skill pack: ./agent-skills.md
- Convert existing code: tubeless-make-pipeline, installed with npx skills add chetmancini/tubeless
- Canonical guide: ./agent-guide.md
- Minimal project: ../examples/tubeless.project.ts
- Project with custom adapters: ../examples/project/tubeless.project.ts
- Maintain stable step IDs.
- For static parameterized step families, keep expansion synchronous and preserve literal IDs with the recipe-local tuple helper in ../examples/parameterized-steps.ts
- Use optional step names only as display overrides; dependencies and selection use IDs.
- Use pipeline.toMermaid() to generate static graph documentation.
- Use tubeless list to enumerate pipelines from defineProject with their names and descriptions. Use stable pipeline IDs with inspect, plan, graph, and run; no command modules are discovered from the filesystem or history. When an error ends with "Did you mean ...?", apply that hint instead of guessing.
- Use tubeless inspect with a registered ID, pipeline, or marked command module for a read-only inventory of identity, targets, metadata, and the default structural plan. Prefer the marked command when both are exported.
- Use tubeless plan with a pipeline or marked command module to preview target, exact-step, and dry-run selection without executing or supplying domain options. Prefer the marked command when both are exported. Use command.plan() or tubeless plan; do not simulate planning with --plan.
- Use tubeless graph with a pipeline or marked command module to print Mermaid without a wrapper script. Prefer the marked command when both are exported. Command files expose the same graph as command.toMermaid().
- Use tubeless run with a project pipeline ID, a uniquely exported schema-backed pipeline, or a definePipelineCommand module; put validated application arguments after --. Explicit commands win, while schema-less or unsupported pipeline inputs require an explicit adapter. Pass --trace for NDJSON traces and --store for SQLite; they compose. --trace - keeps stdout as NDJSON and sends command output to stderr. Programmatic callers implement PipelineTraceExporter at the application edge and compose destinations with composeTraceExporters from tubeless/tracing.
- Use tubeless history to list or show recorded runs from SQLite, or pass --trace to inspect a finished NDJSON artifact without importing it. Studio also accepts --trace as a strictly read-only source. Default print is the projection; --events emits raw NDJSON. Trace files may contain sensitive logs and event payloads.
- Pass full run IDs from scripts; tubeless history also accepts a unique prefix of at least four characters for interactive use, and an ambiguous prefix exits 1.
- Enable shell completion for commands, flags, project pipeline IDs, plan targets and steps, and pipeline command flags with tubeless completion bash, zsh, or fish.
- Set dryRun: "skip" on external side effects, or provide a side-effect-free dryRun handler.
- Use context.log, context.signal, context.sleep, and progress APIs.
- Use createPipelineTestRuntime from tubeless/testing for deterministic tests with captured logs, statuses, progress, clock, and cancellation. Pass overrideStep(step, value) through test-run overrides to supply typed outputs; output schemas still validate and normal step statuses carry outputSource: "override" provenance.
- Import compilePipelineDocument from tubeless/project to compile parsed YAML/JSON with an explicit registry; use compiled.get(id) directly or pass selected pipelines to defineProject. Reuse compiled.metadata for project presentation. Import definePipelineCommand from tubeless/cli for explicit adapters; register each pipeline exactly once, directly or through its command in the same project entry list for CLI and Studio.
- Omit mapOptions only when validated CLI flags already satisfy same-name pipeline options; map renamed, loaded, or derived values explicitly. --step and --target are argv flags; mapOptions and hooks receive stepIds and targets.
- Expose --resume only through managed checkpoint configuration or an explicit resume: true command that handles values.resume. Unsupported commands reject it and omit it from Studio.
- Declare public goals with targets: [step] on definePipeline, then select their
  IDs to include required inputs and failure gates. stepIds is an exact filter
  for any step and cannot be combined with targets.
- Use PipelinePlanStep.selectionReasons for selection explanations; it includes
  target IDs and immediate dependents, so consumers should not rebuild the graph.
- Branch on PipelineError code/phase/kind, not message text. Original thrown
  codes use sourceCode; failed and dependency-blocked reports expose diagnostic metadata.
- A single-goal definePipeline can be { id, steps }: targets defaults to the last step in execution order (use [] to opt out), and finalize defaults to its output or undefined when absent. Unfiltered runs still execute all steps.
- Use requireOutputs for finalizers that need specific completed step outputs.
- Use createSteps(optionsSchema), outputSchema, and resultSchema for optional
  dependency-free Standard Schema validation. run supports async schemas;
  synchronous plan does not invoke schemas.
- Run make check from the package root after package changes.

- Hosted Studio: `tubeless ui --public-url` supports an authenticated application gateway and preserved URL mount. Requires a server-only `TUBELESS_STUDIO_GATEWAY_TOKEN`; application owns every-request admin authorization, fixed upstream, private transport, persistent SQLite, and supervision. One admin trust domain, process-local execution, no automatic mutation retries. See studio.md#host-studio-behind-an-application-gateway.

Advanced:

- In-process agents: ./agents.md (default read/write/edit/bash/list/search tools, custom tools, scripted, OpenAI and Anthropic examples, compatible-API configuration, pipelineTool delegation, shared subtree limits, SQLite checkpoints, and execution environments). The OpenAI helper and `tubeless agent` REPL stay in memory; resume a `defineAgentLoop` or `defineAgent` run with an execution key. See ./agents.md#durable-execution.
- Child pipelines: ./child-pipeline-composition.md
- Remote steps: ./remote-step-composition.md
- Tubeless and Airflow: ./airflow.md
- Tubeless on Temporal: ./temporal.md
- Tubeless on Inngest: ./inngest.md
- Tubeless on Dagster: ./dagster.md
- Tubeless on AWS Step Functions: ./step-functions.md
- Deploy to Cloudflare (Worker, Durable Objects, R2, Access; 14-minute run limit): ./deploy-cloudflare.md
- Public exports: ./api-reference.md
- Machine-readable surface: ./api-report.json
